newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-AJAX RUE MISSED CHANCES AS GRASSHOPPER TOP GROUP A.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AJAX RUE MISSED CHANCES AS GRASSHOPPER TOP GROUP A.

text.p: A thunderous free-kick from Grasshopper Zurich midfielder Murat Yakin stunned Ajax Amsterdam in the Champions' League on Wednesday and kept the unfancied Swiss team on course for their first appearance in the last eight of the European Cup.
Yakin, sporting white trainers, struck with accuracy and venom in the 58th minute, firing an unstoppable free-kick past Edwin van der Sar from over 35 metres.

That was enough to win the Group A encounter which wrote a small footnote in European soccer history. The retractable roof over Ajax's new stadium was closed, making the game the first major European match played "indoors".
Ajax, four times European champions, were left to rue several squandered clearcut chances which highlighted their desperate need for a scorer to replace the injured Patrick Kluivert.
Weakened by injury and the transfer of the core of the side which swept to European glory, Ajax have struggled this season, scoring only five goals in seven league games.

The Dutch champions went into their 99th game in the European Cup without four internationals -- sharpshooter Kluivert, John Veldman, Richard Witschge and Peter Hoekstra -- but skipper Danny Blind was back from injury to marshall the defence, which included Winston Bogarde who played with painkillers in a sore ankle.

The Swiss, who beat Glasgow Rangers 3-0 earlier this month for their first-ever Champions' League win, matched Ajax in the early stages despite the absence of top striker Kubilay Turkyilmaz with a strained calf muscle.

After early sparring Ajax looked likeliest to break the stalemate, with winger Marc Overmars going closest on half an hour after good work on the right by Tijjani Babangida, celebrating his 23rd birthday.
Running clear on goal, the Nigerian squared to Overmars but the winger's low shot rebounded off the post.

Moments later Grasshopper goalkeeper Pascal Zuberbuehler had to be alert to clear at the feet of the advancing Overmars and, as Ajax pressed forward, Kiki Musampa wasted one good chance and then brought another smart save from Zuberbuehler.
But it was by no means one-way traffic.
Romanian Viorel Moldovan, missing Turkyilmaz, his regular strike partner, found space in the Ajax area to fire in a short-range effort but Van der Sar was equal to the shot.
Ajax's Finnish striker Jari Litmanen limped off at halftime and within minutes of the restart Babangida, put through by Ronald de Boer, rounded the goalkeeper but slid his shot wide of an empty net.
Ajax threw caution to the wind and launched an aerial bombardment on Zuberbuehler's goal but the Swiss defence held out for a famous victory beneath the closed roof of Ajax's new space-age stadium.
Three minutes from time Frank de Boer shaved the left post with a curling free-kick from the edge of the box but by then Ajax looked a spent force.
A stunned Ajax coach Louis van Gaal found the defeat hard to swallow: "It is shocking that we lost. We should have won. We should have taken our chances."
Ronald de Boer admitted that Grasshopper had caught out Ajax by playing a 4-5-1 formation with only one man up front.
"We started to play in an un-Ajax-like way, with the long ball. If we'd won we could have afforded to make a mistake. Now we can't," he said.
Teams:

Ajax Amsterdam: 1-Edwin van der Sar; 20-Marcio Santos, 3-Danny Blind, 4-Frank de Boer, 5-Winston Bogarde; 17-Mariano Juan (Mario Melchiot 68th), 10-Jari Litmanen (16-Nordin Wooter 46th), 18-Kiki Musampa, 7-Tijjani Babangida (19-Arnold Scholten 75th), 6-Ronald de Boer, 11-Marc Overmars

Grasshopper Zurich: 1-Pascal Zuberbuehler, 2-Harald Gaemperle, 28-Bernt Haas, 4-Mats Gren, 3-Pascal Thueler; 10-Massimo Lombardo (16-Marcel Koller 89th), 6-Murat Yakin, 7-Antonio Esposito, 14-Johann Vogel; 9-Viorel Moldovan (29-Boris Smiljanic 90th), 19-Joel Magnin (8-Alexandre Comisetti 78th)
